raw_case_text: In the meantime, he was tried with various antiretroviral drugs in combinations, i.e. lamivudine 150-300 mg, zidovudine 300 mg, nevirapine 600 mg, stavudine 20 mg, and tenofovir 300 mg. In 2014-2015, he was prescribed with EFV 600 mg in combination with nevirapine up to 600 mg and lamivudine up to 300 mg at different times. Around this time, the patient presented with decreased sleep, sadness, weeping spells, decreased interaction, decreased appetite, odd behavior, and irrelevant and inappropriate talk at times and had socio-occupational dysfunction. A diagnosis of "bipolar affective disorder, current episode severe depression with psychotic symptoms" was made, and the treatment was started with antidepressant tablet escitalopram 10 mg, which was increased to 20 mg, and antipsychotic olanzapine 5 mg tablet was added to it. This time, he did not improve with the treatment even after 3 months. Hence, olanzapine was discontinued, and tablet quetiapine 50 mg was started which was gradually increased to 300 mg. Electrocardiogram was done periodically while quetiapine was increased and it was found to be normal; no QTc (corrected QT interval of ECG) prolongation was there. As there was no improvement in depression, the antidepressant was changed to another selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, i.e., fluoxetine capsule at a dosage of 20 mg. Still, the patient did not improve at the end of 3 months, and the score on the Beck Depression Inventory was 55 which corresponded to severe depression. The status about lack of any improvement in depression was communicated to the physician who was aware that antiretroviral drugs may cause depression. Hence, he discontinued EFV and started nevirapine. After discontinuing EFV, the patient started to improve in a month and recovered completely in 3 months with good socio-occupational functioning. Quetiapine in the meantime was reduced and stopped (as he complained of increased sedation and found the drug to be costly), and he was continued on fluoxetine 20 mg and aripiprazole 2.5 mg. The score on the Beck Depression Inventory at the end of 3 months was 6 which corresponded to minimal depression.

subjective.chief_complaint: A male patient presenting with severe depression, decreased sleep, weeping spells, anorexia, social withdrawal, odd behavior, and inappropriate speech refractory to psychiatric therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with progressive psychiatric decompensation characterized by decreased sleep, persistent sadness, weeping spells, social withdrawal, anorexia, odd behavior, and inappropriate speech with marked socio-occupational impairment. The depressive episode began following modification of his antiretroviral therapy regimen in 2014-2015 to include efavirenz 600 mg daily. The depression proved refractory to successive antidepressant and antipsychotic trials, including escitalopram (titrated to 20 mg), olanzapine (5 mg), quetiapine (titrated to 300 mg), and fluoxetine (20 mg), with persistence of severe depression (Beck Depression Inventory score of 55) over more than six months.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of bipolar affective disorder; treated with sequential antiretroviral regimens including lamivudine 150-300 mg, zidovudine 300 mg, nevirapine 600 mg, stavudine 20 mg, and tenofovir 300 mg, followed by efavirenz 600 mg daily in combination with nevirapine and lamivudine.
subjective.review_of_systems: Decreased sleep, decreased appetite, sadness, weeping spells, social withdrawal, odd behavior, inappropriate speech; excessive sedation reported while taking quetiapine.

objective.physical_examination: Mental status examination: Profound depressive affect, weeping spells, psychomotor slowing, social withdrawal, odd behavior, and occasional irrelevant and inappropriate speech.
objective.routine_investigations: Serial electrocardiograms (ECGs): Normal tracing with normal corrected QT interval (no QTc prolongation) during quetiapine titration. Beck Depression Inventory (BDI): Admission/refractory score of 55 (severe depression); declined to 6 (minimal depression) after treatment modification.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Efavirenz-induced severe depression with psychotic symptoms in a patient with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection and underlying bipolar affective disorder.
Plan & Outcome: Due to lack of response to escitalopram, olanzapine, quetiapine, and fluoxetine, efavirenz was identified as the offending neuropsychiatric agent and discontinued, replacing it with nevirapine. Following efavirenz cessation, the patient showed clinical improvement within one month and achieved full remission at three months with restored socio-occupational functioning. Psychotropic therapy was rationalized to fluoxetine 20 mg and aripiprazole 2.5 mg daily (quetiapine was tapered and discontinued due to sedation and cost). Beck Depression Inventory score decreased from 55 to 6.
